content:
Yesterday we saw the giants that stand along the narrow way; forgiving betrayal, loving the unloving, killing pride, controlling the tongue, staying pure, and serving without appreciation. Ten men looked at those giants and said, "We are not able." We ended asking what one man said in answer to all that fear. Today we hear his voice.

Numbers 13:30 says, "But Caleb tried to quiet the people as they stood before Moses. 'Let's go at once to take the land,' he said. 'We can certainly conquer it!'" Caleb did not deny the facts. He did not say there were no giants. He did not say the cities had no walls. He did not pretend the path was easy. But he looked beyond the difficulty to Yahweh's promise. His faith was not blind to the challenge; his faith was simply greater than the challenge. And that is the spirit the New Creation must have. We must not pretend that there are no trials.

We must not say the narrow way is easy. We must not hide the cost of discipleship. But neither must we ever speak as though the giants are greater than Yahweh. Paul says, "For I can do everything through Christ, who gives me strength" (Philippians 4:13). And John says, "For every child of God defeats this evil world, and we achieve this victory through our faith" (1 John 5:4).

Caleb's words were beautifully simple: let us go up at once. Faith does not delay obedience. Fear says, "Wait." Fear says, "Later." Fear says, "Let us think of another way." But faith says, "If Yahweh has spoken, let us obey now." This is very practical for us. When Yahweh shows us a wrong habit, Caleb's mind should say, "Let us remove it at once." When Yahweh shows us we must forgive someone, Caleb's mind should say, "Let us go and make peace at once." When Yahweh shows us we must leave a worldly practice, Caleb's mind should say, "Let us obey at once." When Yahweh shows us we must serve, preach, pray, or sacrifice, Caleb's mind should say, "Let us go up at once." For delaying obedience only gives fear the time it needs to grow.

And Caleb was not left standing alone. Joshua stood with him. Numbers 14:6 says, "Two of the men who had explored the land, Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh, tore their clothing." Joshua and Caleb had seen the very same land as the ten spies. They had walked the same paths. They had seen the same Anakim and the same fortified cities. But they did not allow fear to rule them. In Numbers 14:8-9 they said, "If the LORD is pleased with us, he will bring us safely into that land and give it to us. Do not rebel against the LORD, and don't be afraid of the people of the land." Notice their confidence was not in themselves. They did not say, "We are strong enough." They said, "If Yahweh is pleased with us, He will bring us safely into that land." This is true faith. Faith does not boast in human strength. Faith rests in God’s power. And they added a solemn warning: do not rebel, and do not be afraid. For fear can become rebellion. When fear makes us refuse obedience, it is no longer merely fear; it has become resistance against God.

This is the voice the flock needs today. Not the voice of panic. Not the voice of unbelief. Not the voice that makes the people weak. The flock needs the voice of Caleb and Joshua saying, "Do not rebel. Do not fear. God is with us." And notice something precious in the wording. Numbers 13:30 says Caleb "tried to quiet the people." That itself is a great service. A faithful servant does not increase panic; he quiets panic. He brings the mind of the people back to God. He does not deny the problem, but he refuses to let the problem become greater than the promise.

There is always danger when fearful people speak loudly among the flock. The ten spies did not merely fear privately. They spread their fear publicly. Numbers 13:32 says, "So they spread this bad report about the land among the Israelites." This is very dangerous. One fearful heart can become ten fearful voices, and ten fearful voices can trouble a whole congregation. A bad report can create panic, distress, and stumbling among the people of God. And this still happens today. A few may say, "This truth is too hard." Others may say, "This separation is too much." Some may say, "This narrow way will cost us too much." Some may say, "We cannot live like Christ in this world." Some may say, "If we obey fully, people will hate us." And slowly the spirit of fear spreads. Instead of encouraging the flock to trust God, they fill the flock with anxiety. This is why our words matter so much. Proverbs 18:21 says, "The tongue can bring death or life." A Caleb-like word strengthens faith. A spy-like bad report weakens faith. A Joshua-like voice says, "Yahweh is able." A fear-filled voice says, "We cannot." One kind of speech helps the flock move forward. The other kind makes the flock tremble at the very border of the promise.

But now we must go back and pick up something the spies were still holding in their hands as they spoke. Even while their mouths were spreading fear, their arms were carrying the proof that God had told the truth. There was a great cluster of grapes on a pole between two men. There were figs. There were pomegranates. God did not choose those three fruits by accident. Each one carries a meaning, and together they show us exactly what kind of inheritance is waiting for the New Creation. What do the grapes, the figs, and the pomegranates teach us? That is where we will continue tomorrow.

title: Prayer
text:
O Yahweh, our Father,

Give us the mond of Caleb, who saw the giants yet trusted Your promise above them.

Teach us not to delay obedience, for delay only gives fear time to grow in us.

Make us voices that quiet panic among the brethren, and never voices that spread it.

Guard our tongues, for they can bring death or life to those who hear us.

And keep our fear from ever hardening into rebellion against You.

"Be strong and courageous! Do not be afraid, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go." - Joshua 1:9

In Christ name we pray. Amen.
